items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The dialect code is clean and matches the existing builder style. However, the dialect business logic uses the single-letter callback name `w` (`windows.map((w) => sql`${sql.identifier(w.name)} ...`)`, `findIndex((w) => w.name === name)`), which triggers the cap. The new public `.window()` methods have no doc comments, unlike nearby builder methods.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The spec builder is shared (`buildWindowSpecSql`). But the same 25-line `window()` body, with proxy-callback resolution and replace-or-push logic, is copied into all five select builders. That goes against the 'thin .window() method' convention. The WINDOW clause block is also repeated in each dialect.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `validateWindowName` runs at the builder boundary. The tests cover non-empty and whitespace names, inverted frames (/from/), and ntile and boundary validation, and all hidden tests passed (130/130). A repeated window name replaces the earlier definition on purpose, with no error swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive. It adds an optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` to each *SelectConfig and the same `.window()` method to pg, mysql, sqlite, singlestore and gel. `windowSql` is undefined when no windows are set, so queries without windows produce the same SQL. P2P tests all passed (566/566).
